purplecomet-ms-2026-01.title: Angle sum
purplecomet-ms-2026-01.body:
The angles of a hexagon add to $(6-2)\cdot180^\circ = 720^\circ$. So $90 + 5x = 720$ and $x = 126$.

**Answer: 126**

purplecomet-ms-2026-01.title: Exterior angles
purplecomet-ms-2026-01.body:
The exterior angles add to $360^\circ$: $90 + 5(180 - x) = 360$, so $180 - x = 54$ and $x = 126$.

**Answer: 126**

purplecomet-ms-2026-02.title: Multiply the factors
purplecomet-ms-2026-02.body:
The price becomes $0.9 \cdot 0.8 = 0.72$ of the original, a discount of $28$ percent.

**Answer: 28**

purplecomet-ms-2026-02.title: Try a price
purplecomet-ms-2026-02.body:
Start at $\$100$: Monday $\$90$, Tuesday $90 - 18 = \$72$. That is $\$28$ off, i.e. $28$ percent.

**Answer: 28**

purplecomet-ms-2026-03.title: Count by length
purplecomet-ms-2026-03.body:
The leading digit is $2$ or $6$.
- 1 digit: $2$ numbers; 2 digits: $2\cdot3 = 6$; 3 digits: $2\cdot 9 = 18$.
- 4 digits up to $2026$: must start $20$, then the third digit is $0$ or $2$ and the last any of $3$: $2000, 2002, 2006, 2020, 2022, 2026$ — $6$ numbers.

Total $2 + 6 + 18 + 6 = 32$.

**Answer: 32**

purplecomet-ms-2026-03.title: Leading zeros
purplecomet-ms-2026-03.body:
Write numbers as 4-digit strings. Strings starting with $0$: $3^3 = 27$, minus $0000$: $26$. Strings starting with $2$ and at most $2026$: $20\_\_$ with third digit $0$ or $2$: $6$. Total $32$.

**Answer: 32**

purplecomet-ms-2026-04.title: Subtract
purplecomet-ms-2026-04.body:
The inside rectangle is $(20 - 2 - 4)\times(16 - 1 - 3) = 14\times12$. Shaded area $= 320 - 168 = 152$.

**Answer: 152**

purplecomet-ms-2026-04.title: Cut into strips
purplecomet-ms-2026-04.body:
Extend the top and bottom of the inner rectangle: the shaded region becomes strips of areas $20\cdot1$ (bottom), $20\cdot3$ (top), $2\cdot12$ (left), $4\cdot12$ (right): $20 + 60 + 24 + 48 = 152$.

**Answer: 152**

purplecomet-ms-2026-05.title: Factor
purplecomet-ms-2026-05.body:
$x^2 + 5x - 204 = (x + 17)(x - 12) < 0$ exactly when $-17 < x < 12$. The integers $-16, \dots, 11$ number $28$.

**Answer: 28**

purplecomet-ms-2026-06.title: Simplify
purplecomet-ms-2026-06.body:
The left side is $\frac{4053n}{3n} = 1351$; the right side is $5n + 1$. So $5n = 1350$ and $n = 270$.

**Answer: 270**

purplecomet-ms-2026-07.title: Work mod 8
purplecomet-ms-2026-07.body:
Odd squares are $\equiv 1 \pmod 8$, and $2^2 = 4$. If $k$ of the primes equal $2$, the sum is $\equiv 4k + (7 - k) = 3k + 7 \pmod 8$, which must be $\equiv 1$; so $3k \equiv 2$, $k \equiv 6 \pmod 8$, so $k = 6$.

Then $24 + q^2 = p^2$ for an odd prime $q$: $(p - q)(p + q) = 24$ with both factors even: $(2, 12)$ gives $q = 5$, $p = 7$; $(4, 6)$ gives $q = 1$, not prime. So the primes are six 2s and a 5 ($24 + 25 = 49$), and the sum is $12 + 5 = 17$.

**Answer: 17**

purplecomet-ms-2026-08.title: Relative speeds
purplecomet-ms-2026-08.body:
Going forward she gains on the front at $4 - 2 = 2$ km/h, so covering the $100$ m gap takes $\frac{100}{2000} = \frac1{20}$ h, during which she walks $4000\cdot\frac1{20} = 200$ m. Going back the gap closes at $6$ km/h: $\frac{100}{6000} = \frac1{60}$ h, and she walks $\frac{4000}{60} = \frac{200}{3}$ m. Total $\frac{800}{3}$ m, so $m + n = 803$.

**Answer: 803**

purplecomet-ms-2026-08.title: Total time
purplecomet-ms-2026-08.body:
Her total time is $\frac1{20} + \frac1{60} = \frac1{15}$ hour at $4$ km/h the whole time, so she walks $\frac{4000}{15} = \frac{800}{3}$ meters. Answer $803$.

**Answer: 803**

purplecomet-ms-2026-09.title: Count green faces
purplecomet-ms-2026-09.body:
There are $6\cdot100 = 600$ green small faces in total. Each small face ends up on top with probability $\frac16$, so by linearity the expected number of green tops is $\frac{600}{6} = 100$.

**Answer: 100**

purplecomet-ms-2026-09.title: Classify cubes
purplecomet-ms-2026-09.body:
$8$ corner cubes (3 green faces), $12\cdot8 = 96$ edge cubes (2 green faces), $6\cdot64 = 384$ face cubes (1 green face). Expected value $8\cdot\frac36 + 96\cdot\frac26 + 384\cdot\frac16 = 4 + 32 + 64 = 100$.

**Answer: 100**

purplecomet-ms-2026-10.title: Weighted average
purplecomet-ms-2026-10.body:
If a fraction $f$ passed, $76f + 42(1 - f) = 60$, so $34f = 18$ and $f = \frac9{17}$. So $m + n = 26$.

**Answer: 26**

purplecomet-ms-2026-10.title: Balance distances
purplecomet-ms-2026-10.body:
The mean $60$ is $16$ below $76$ and $18$ above $42$. The groups balance, so passers : failers $= 18 : 16 = 9 : 8$, and $\frac{9}{17}$ passed. Answer $26$.

**Answer: 26**

purplecomet-ms-2026-11.title: Two cases
purplecomet-ms-2026-11.body:
Prime digits: $2, 3, 5, 7$ ($4$ of them); non-prime digits: $6$ ($0,1,4,6,8,9$), of which $5$ are allowed as a leading digit. There are $9000$ four-digit numbers.
- First digit prime: $4$ choices, one of the other three positions prime ($3\cdot4$), the other two non-prime ($6^2$): $4\cdot12\cdot36 = 1728$.
- First digit non-prime ($5$ choices): two of the last three prime ($3\cdot 4^2$), the last non-prime ($6$): $5\cdot48\cdot6 = 1440$.

Probability $\frac{3168}{9000} = \frac{44}{125}$, so $m + n = 169$.

**Answer: 169**

purplecomet-ms-2026-12.title: Complete the square
purplecomet-ms-2026-12.body:
$x(s - x) = \frac{s^2}{4} - \left(x - \frac s2\right)^2 \le \frac{s^2}4$. The terms are independent, so the maximum is $\frac{1 + 9 + 25 + 49}{4} = \frac{84}{4} = 21$, at $a, b, c, d = \frac12, \frac32, \frac52, \frac72$.

**Answer: 21**

purplecomet-ms-2026-12.title: Vertex of each parabola
purplecomet-ms-2026-12.body:
Each $x(s - x)$ is a downward parabola with roots $0$ and $s$, so its maximum is at $x = \frac s2$: values $\frac14, \frac94, \frac{25}4, \frac{49}4$, total $21$.

**Answer: 21**

purplecomet-ms-2026-13.title: Symmetry of binomial coefficients
purplecomet-ms-2026-13.body:
If $|S| = n$, then $\binom n8 = \binom n{13} > 0$. The values $\binom nk$ strictly increase up to the middle and then decrease symmetrically, so two different $k$ give the same value only when they add to $n$: $n = 8 + 13 = 21$. Casey circled $\binom{21}{2} = 210$ subsets.

**Answer: 210**

purplecomet-ms-2026-15.title: Similar triangles
purplecomet-ms-2026-15.body:
The line from the corner cuts off similar triangles at the four strip heights, with areas in ratio $1 : 4 : 9 : 16$. Let $Y$ have area $1$; then the triangle up to the top of the square has area $16$ and up to the third line $9$, so $W = 16 - 9 = 7$ and $X = 3\cdot7 = 21$. Each strip has area $W + X = 28$, so $Z = 28 - 1 = 27$, and $n = 27$.

**Answer: 27**

purplecomet-ms-2026-15.title: Coordinates
purplecomet-ms-2026-15.body:
Let the square have side $1$ and let the line cross the first strip line at horizontal distance $x$ from the left side. It then crosses the lines at $x, 2x, 3x$ and the top at $4x$. In the top strip, $W$ is a trapezoid with parallel sides $3x, 4x$ and $X$ has $1 - 4x$, $1 - 3x$, so $\frac{2 - 7x}{7x} = 3$, $x = \frac1{14}$. In the bottom strip, $Y$ is a triangle of base $x$ and $Z$ a trapezoid with sides $1 - x$ and $1$: $\frac ZY = \frac{2 - x}{x} = 27$.

**Answer: 27**

purplecomet-ms-2026-16.title: Share as much as possible
purplecomet-ms-2026-16.body:
$B$ has sum $2520$. Let $k$ be the number of elements of $A$ not in $B$, with sum $s$. The union has $36 + k$ elements and sum $2520 + s$.
- If $k = 25$ (disjoint), the mean is $\frac{2520 + 1250}{61} > 61$.
- If $k \le 24$: $s \ge 1 + 2 + \cdots + k = \frac{k(k+1)}{2}$, so the mean is at least $g(k) = \frac{2520 + k(k+1)/2}{36 + k}$. Adding one more element (from $k$ to $k+1$) adds at most $k + 1 \le 25$ to the numerator, which is below the current mean (always more than $\frac{2520}{60} = 42$), so $g$ decreases in $k$. The minimum is $g(24) = \frac{2520 + 300}{60} = 47$.

It is achieved by $A = \{1, 2, \dots, 24, 950\}$ (sum $1250$) and $B = \{27, 28, \dots, 60, 91, 950\}$ (sum $1479 + 91 + 950 = 2520$): the union has $60$ elements with sum $2820$, mean $47$.

**Answer: 47**

purplecomet-ms-2026-17.title: Four corner triangles
purplecomet-ms-2026-17.body:
The union is $S$ plus four congruent right triangles (the corners of $S'$ sticking out), each with legs $x, y$ and hypotenuse $h$ equal to a side of the octagon. Each side of $S'$ is $x + y + h = 16$, and the area gives $256 + 2xy = 288$, so $xy = 16$.

From $h = 16 - (x + y)$: $x^2 + y^2 = 256 - 32(x+y) + (x+y)^2$, so $0 = 256 - 32(x + y) + 2xy = 288 - 32(x + y)$, giving $x + y = 9$ and $h = 7$. The octagon's $8$ sides are all hypotenuses, so its perimeter is $56$.

**Answer: 56**

purplecomet-ms-2026-18.title: Vieta and the discriminant
purplecomet-ms-2026-18.body:
$(x_1 + 1)(x_2 + 1) = x_1x_2 + x_1 + x_2 + 1 = \frac n{10} - \frac m{10} + 1 = 1$, so $n = m$. Rational roots need $m^2 - 40m = s^2$ for an integer $s \ge 0$, i.e. $(m - 20)^2 - s^2 = 400$, so $(m - 20 - s)(m - 20 + s) = 400$ with both factors of the same parity, hence both even.

The largest $m$ comes from the factor pair $(2, 200)$: $m - 20 = 101$, $m = 121$. (Check: $10x^2 + 121x + 121$ has discriminant $14641 - 4840 = 9801 = 99^2$, roots $-\frac{11}{10}$ and $-11$; $(-\frac1{10})(-10) = 1$ ✓.) So $m + n = 242$.

**Answer: 242**

purplecomet-ms-2026-19.title: Fix one red plate
purplecomet-ms-2026-19.body:
Only the red positions matter. Fix one red plate's position; the other $14$ positions, read around the circle, hold $4$ reds (R) and $10$ others (O), all $\binom{14}{4}$ patterns equally likely. We need the string to start and end with O and have no two R's adjacent: start from $\mathrm{ORORORORO}$ and distribute the remaining $5$ O's into the $5$ O-blocks: $\binom{9}{4} = 126$ ways.

Probability $\frac{126}{1001} = \frac{18}{143}$, so $m + n = 161$.

**Answer: 161**

purplecomet-ms-2026-19.title: Gaps on a circle
purplecomet-ms-2026-19.body:
The red positions are a random $5$-subset of $15$ positions in a circle: $\binom{15}5 = 3003$. Non-adjacent $5$-subsets of a $15$-cycle: $\frac{15}{15 - 5}\binom{10}{5} = 378$. Probability $\frac{378}{3003} = \frac{18}{143}$; answer $161$.

**Answer: 161**

purplecomet-ms-2026-20.title: Prism plus pyramid
purplecomet-ms-2026-20.body:
The intersection is bounded below by $ABCD$, on the $AB$ side by plane $ABH$, on the $CD$ side by plane $CDG$, and on the other two sides by planes $BCH$ and $ADH$ (these lie below $BCG$, $ADG$). Let plane $CDG$ meet $BH$ and $AH$ at $J$ and $K$; the solid has faces $ABCD$, $\triangle BCJ$, $\triangle ADK$ and trapezoids $ABJK$, $CDKJ$.

**Cross-section through $E, F, G, H$.** Put $E = 0$, $F = 6$ on a horizontal axis. Line $EH$ has height $\frac{3}{6}t$ and line $FG$ has height $\frac56(6 - t)$; they meet where $\frac t2 = 5 - \frac{5t}{6}$, i.e. $t = \frac{15}{4}$ at height $L = \frac{15}{8}$ (the top edge $JK$).

**Length of $JK$.** $JK$ is parallel to $AB$ in triangle $ABH$, at height $\frac{15}8$ out of $3$, so $JK = 6\left(1 - \frac{15/8}{3}\right) = \frac94$.

**Volume.** Cutting perpendicular to $JK$ at $J$ and $K$: the middle part is a prism with cross-section a triangle of base $6$ and height $\frac{15}8$, length $\frac94$: $\frac12\cdot6\cdot\frac{15}8\cdot\frac94 = \frac{405}{32}$. The two end parts fit together into a pyramid with a $\left(6 - \frac94\right)\times 6$ rectangular base and height $\frac{15}{8}$: $\frac13\cdot\frac{15}4\cdot6\cdot\frac{15}8 = \frac{225}{16}$.

Total $\frac{405}{32} + \frac{450}{32} = \frac{855}{32}$, so $m + n = 887$.

**Answer: 887**
